description: Let this application send email now, while the project is still being written, so a welcome or a password reset is built and tested against the real thing instead of being left out or sending the user to open a Resend account and verify a domain. There is nothing to sign up for. Safe to call twice. Only for a project that sends mail: skip it otherwise, and skip it when the project already sets a RESEND_API_KEY of its own (409 own_email). A 503 email_unavailable means email is not set up on this server: carry on without it and tell the user. If the call is refused or blocked, do not look for another route: tell the user. The token is not returned: call `email_env_to_file` to put the variables in .env. Send with the `resend` package written as for any Resend account: new Resend(process.env.RESEND_API_KEY), then resend.emails.send({ from: process.env.EMAIL_FROM, to, subject, html }); in Python resend.api_key = os.environ['RESEND_API_KEY']. The package reads RESEND_BASE_URL or RESEND_API_URL, which point at the platform's relay. The message always leaves from the application's own address under the platform's sending domain, whatever `from` says, with the application's name as the display name, and nothing receives replies at that address, so set reply_to (replyTo in Node) to a real one if people may answer. It is transactional mail: at most five addresses on a message, a limited number a day by the owner's plan (fewer for an account only days old), and a 429 with daily_quota_exceeded or rate_limit_exceeded means try later, so show a person a message and do not retry in a loop. Attachments, scheduled sending, templates and resend.batch.send are refused. Never use it for newsletters or bulk mail. Tell the user what was set up and on which account.
name: email_create
title: Let the application send email now
